script: [serious] January 15th, 1919. Boston. Just after noon, witnesses heard a sound like machine-gun fire. Rivets, bursting out of a steel tank fifty feet tall. Inside it: two point three million gallons of molasses. In seconds, a wave up to twenty-five feet high tore through the North End at thirty-five miles an hour. It flattened buildings. It swept away wagons, horses, people. Then the air cooled... and the molasses thickened like glue. [whispers] Rescuers couldn't pull people free. Twenty-one people died. About a hundred and fifty were hurt. And here's what makes it worse. The tank had leaked from the start. The fix? Paint it brown, so the leaks wouldn't show. Neighbors used to collect the dripping molasses to take home. After three years in court, the company was found liable. And for decades, locals swore that on hot summer days... the North End still smelled sweet. This is Dossier Decoded. Case file number two. Which file should we open next?
